purpose: Compare the average decline in vaccine effectiveness against infection and severe disease without using generated geometry that could imply false numerical precision.
title: Protection wanes faster against infection than severe disease
subtitle: Average decline from month 1 to month 6 · pre-Omicron systematic review
story: Effectiveness against infection declined by 21.0 percentage points on average.
Effectiveness against severe disease declined by 10.0 percentage points on average.
Circulating immune memory, limited airway immunity and variant escape are supported explanations, but the studies do not assign a percentage to each cause.
layout_notes: Use two equal-area aligned rows, one for infection and one for severe disease; row area must not encode magnitude.
Use large black numerals, small coloured outcome markers, and thin grey separators; no rounded cards.
Place three concise supported explanations in one quiet column using simple labelled biological marks, not decorative icons.
Use a compact bottom key without a glossary badge or book symbol.
constraints: Do not draw an axis, bar, dot, whisker or other quantitative geometry.
Keep the two evidence rows exactly the same size.
Do not imply that the three explanations quantitatively partition the decline.
exact_text: Average decline from month 1 to month 6 · pre-Omicron systematic review
Equal row sizes do not encode magnitude
B and T cells can limit progression after infection
Injected vaccine elicits limited local airway immunity
Changed spike can evade existing antibodies
Percentage point = absolute change in percentages
